title: OpenAI Countersues Apple, Accusing It of Stealing Secrets and Pressuring Suppliers
yt_title: OpenAI Countersues Apple: Stolen Secrets and Supplier Threats?
yt_description:
OpenAI just hit back at Apple in court. In a countersuit filed November 27 in federal court in San Jose, OpenAI accuses Apple of trade secret theft, interfering with contracts and pressuring hardware suppliers that work for both companies. Apple's own lawsuit against OpenAI, its device unit io and two ex-Apple engineers is headed for trial on July 19, 2027.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! The AI war just moved to the courtroom: OpenAI is suing Apple! On Friday, November twenty seventh, OpenAI filed a countersuit against Apple in federal court in San Jose, California. The claims? Trade secret theft, interference with contracts, and unfair competition under California law. OpenAI says Apple stole its secrets, and is coercing and threatening suppliers that build hardware for both companies. According to the filing, Apple asked shared factories to name the people working on OpenAI projects, and pushed at least one vendor to stop the work. Ouch! OpenAI also claims Apple's exit rules are trapdoors, built to accuse anyone who leaves of stealing. And the motive? OpenAI says Apple has struggled to add new AI to its once popular products. Now, rewind. Apple fired first, back in July, suing OpenAI, its hardware unit io, and two former Apple engineers. Apple says confidential hardware files walked out the door, straight into OpenAI's secret device project. Remember, OpenAI bought Jony Ive's design firm io last year, to build new personal AI gadgets. OpenAI denies all of it. It says Apple's lawsuit is really about stopping engineers from switching teams. In October, OpenAI said a former employee went back to Apple with more than one hundred confidential files about its unreleased hardware. Apple says its own investigation found no OpenAI secrets, and asked for more details. Meanwhile, a judge said the court is highly likely to grant Apple a preliminary injunction. Big pressure! Apple's original case is set for trial on July nineteenth, twenty twenty seven. So grab some popcorn, this one is long. Want every detail?
